title: Balanced Binary Tree
keyIdea: Balanced means at every node the two subtree heights differ by at most 1. Compute heights bottom-up (like Max Depth) and check abs(left − right) > 1 at each node on the way back up: one pass, O(n).

approaches.name: Top-down: height at every node
approaches.idea: At each node compute both heights from scratch, check the difference, then recurse into both children.
approaches.why: height() is called again for every node's subtree: O(n²) on a chain, O(n log n) when balanced.

approaches.name: Bottom-up: one pass
approaches.idea: maxDepth returns the height as usual and sets isBalanced = false if abs(right − left) > 1 at any node.
approaches.why: Each node's height is computed once and used by its parent.

quiz.q: Is checking only the root's two heights enough?
options: No: every node must be within 1, a deeper node can break it
Only if the root has two children

quiz.q: Why is the bottom-up version O(n)?
options: Each height is computed once and reused by the parent
No: at node 1 the left height is 2 and the right is 0
